results.fact: Difficulty of the Gardner-North Gardner connecting ridge
results.correct_value: Crest between Gardner and Point 8487: class 3-4 over gendarmes if taken direct (a lower bypass under the cliffs avoids it); Point 8487 to North Gardner: mostly class 2
results.evidence: Two descriptions agree the traverse from Point 8487 to North Gardner does not exceed class 2 (one tracked party calls it all class 2), while the crest between Gardner and Point 8487 ('Gardner Traverse') has pinnacles/tricky scrambling rated class 3-4 with a safer drop to ~7,400 ft under the cliffs; another party met some 4th class when off-line on the ridge. beta and descent_text each described only one half; both now name both sections.

results.fact: Direction from Gardner summit toward North Gardner / Point 8,487
results.correct_value: From Gardner's summit the ridge runs WEST down to the low point, then north over Point 8487 to North Gardner (which lies about a mile NW overall)

results.correct_value: Pass at the Wolf Creek Trailhead ($5/day, $30 annual, NW Forest Pass or Interagency honored); no Cutthroat Lake rule; the WA-20 pass closure does not block the Winthrop-side drive
results.evidence: The Forest Service page for the Wolf Creek Trailhead lists $5/day or $30 annual, honoring the Northwest Forest Pass and Interagency passes; a second route description also says a NW Forest Pass is required at this trailhead. WSDOT gates the winter closure between MP 134 and the Silver Star gate (MP 171) near Mazama, west of Winthrop, from which the trailhead is reached via Twin Lakes and Wolf Creek roads. Cutthroat Lake is a Washington Pass-area lake unrelated to this route.
